## Eight common assumptions, negated

| # | Common assumption | If it were false, the conditional effect would be… |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | A residual bypass (edge 3 = skip) mainly makes optimisation easier, so convs on deep edges gain from it. | The identity path is redundant with the deep path, or it dominates the sum, so deep 3x3 convs gain less or are muted. |
| A2 | Parallel 3x3 convs that merge at the same node are redundant. | They complement each other: one is shallow and one is a deeper conv(conv) branch, so the second conv gains more. |
| A3 | Pooling hurts no matter what it pools. | Pooling learned conv features works as smoothing or regularisation, so avg_pool after a conv hurts less or even helps. |
| A4 | A 1x1 conv on edge 3 only matters because it removes the identity shortcut. | If another identity route exists (for example 0→1→3), giving up the edge-3 shortcut costs much less. |
| A5 | A deep-path conv works equally well whatever input-side op feeds its source node. | An upstream pool or identity acts as a bottleneck, so a downstream 3x3 extracts less from pooled features. |
| A6 | An upgrade to edge 0 is valuable only through the deep path. | Edge 0 also feeds the output through edge 4, so its value depends on edge 4 and on whether edge 3 already supplies features. |
| A7 | Skip connections on deep edges are neutral fillers. | A skip on edge 4 or 5 forwards a convolved node straight to the output, so it acts as a conv branch whose value depends on upstream ops. |
| A8 | Interactions keep the same sign on easy and hard datasets. | Capacity matters more on ImageNet16-120 and CIFAR-100, so interactions that involve capacity strengthen there. The hypotheses below are restricted to cases where the sign plausibly holds on all three datasets. |

## Constraint checks

- **Gap 4 (same-edge replacement):** this is banned pattern 1, so I reframed it as edit 3 → nor_conv_1x1 conditioned on whether an alternative shortcut exists (edge 0) or whether the deep path is conv-heavy (edge 5).
- **No inert conditions:** none of the conditions makes the edited edge unreachable. For example, edits on edges 2 and 4 are never conditioned on edge 0 = none, and edits feeding node 2 are never conditioned on edge 5 = none.
- **Condition reuse:** each condition setting appears in at most two hypotheses.
